1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	**Show Command Center** — a trade show project management tool for Exhibitor Services teams at General Service Contractors. Built as a pnpm monorepo with a React frontend, Express backend, and PostgreSQL database.
8	
9	## Common Commands
10	
11	```bash
12	# Build & typecheck
13	pnpm run build                  # Typecheck + build all packages
14	pnpm run typecheck              # Full typecheck across all packages
15	
16	# Development
17	pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run dev           # Build (esbuild) then start API server (no watch; restart to pick up changes)
18	pnpm --filter @workspace/show-command-center run dev  # Start frontend (Vite HMR)
19	
20	# Database
21	pnpm --filter @workspace/db run generate  # Generate new migration
22	pnpm --filter @workspace/db run migrate   # Apply migrations
23	pnpm --filter @workspace/db run push      # Push schema directly (dev only, no migration file)
24	
25	# API code generation (run after editing lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml)
26	pnpm --filter @workspace/api-spec run codegen
27	
28	# Testing (requires both servers already running on port 80)
29	pnpm --filter @workspace/show-command-center run test              # All Playwright tests
30	pnpm --filter @workspace/show-command-center run test:ui           # Playwright UI mode
31	pnpm --filter @workspace/show-command-center run test -- --grep "test name"  # Single test by name
32	pnpm --filter @workspace/show-command-center run test -- tests/smoke.spec.ts # Single file
33	```
34	
35	## Architecture
36	
37	### Monorepo Layout
38	
39	```
40	artifacts/          # Deployable applications
41	  api-server/       # Express 5 backend
42	  show-command-center/  # React 19 + Vite frontend
43	  mockup-sandbox/   # Component preview tool
44	
45	lib/                # Shared packages
46	  db/               # Drizzle ORM schema & migrations (PostgreSQL)
47	  api-spec/         # OpenAPI spec (source of truth for the API contract)
48	  api-client-react/ # React Query hooks generated from OpenAPI
49	  api-zod/          # Zod schemas generated from OpenAPI
50	```
51	
52	### Data Flow
53	
54	```
55	api-spec/openapi.yaml
56	    → (orval codegen) →
57	api-client-react/ (React Query hooks) + api-zod/ (Zod schemas)
58	    ↑ implemented by ↑
59	api-server/ (Express routes)
60	    ↓ uses ↓
61	db/ (Drizzle ORM + schema → drizzle-zod types)
62	    ↓ uses ↓
63	PostgreSQL 16
64	```
65	
66	### OpenAPI-First Development
67	
68	The API contract lives in `lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml`. After modifying it, run `pnpm --filter @workspace/api-spec run codegen` to regenerate:
69	- `lib/api-client-react/src/generated/api.ts` — React Query hooks used in the frontend
70	- `lib/api-zod/src/generated/` — Zod schemas for request/response validation
71	
72	### Frontend Pages
73	
74	| Route | Component | Purpose |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| `/` | Dashboard | Show cards, "Next Up" banner, overdue items |
77	| `/calendar` | Calendar | Monthly view with color-coded show chips |
78	| `/shows/:id` | Show Detail | Tabs: Tasks, E-Blasts, Links |
79	| `/office-tasks` | OfficeTasks | Office-wide task management |
80	
81	### Backend Routes
82	
83	All routes are under `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/`: `/shows`, `/shows/:showId/tasks`, `/shows/:showId/eblasts`, `/shows/:showId/links`, `/calendar`, `/dashboard/summary`, `/dashboard/overdue`, `/office-tasks`, `/venues`, `/export`.
84	
85	The `/export` route returns ICS (iCalendar) format for importing shows into calendar apps.
86	
87	The API server runs DB migrations automatically on startup (via `drizzle-orm/node-postgres/migrator`), but only if the `shows` table does not yet exist — otherwise it skips to avoid re-applying already-applied migrations.
88	
89	## Environment Variables
90	
91	| Variable | Required by |
92	|---|---|
93	| `DATABASE_URL` | API server + DB migrations |
94	| `PORT` | API server + Vite frontend dev server |
95	| `BASE_PATH` | Vite frontend base path |
96	| `NODE_ENV` | API server |
97	
98	## Key Conventions
99	
100	- **Package manager**: pnpm only — a `preinstall` script enforces this.
101	- **Node version**: 24; **TypeScript**: 5.9.
102	- **Zod imports**: Use `zod/v4` — all schemas in this repo import from `"zod/v4"`, not `"zod"`.
103	- **Workspace deps**: Use `workspace:*` to reference local packages.
104	- **DB types**: Drizzle-zod auto-generates Zod schemas from the DB schema; use these rather than writing them by hand.
105	- **UI components**: Radix UI primitives + custom wrappers in `artifacts/show-command-center/src/components/ui/`.
106	- **Routing**: wouter (not React Router).
107	- **Logging**: Pino with HTTP middleware on the server.
108	
109	## Domain Logic
110	
111	### Urgency System
112	
113	Show urgency is based on days until `moveInDate` (see `getUrgencyInfo` in `artifacts/show-command-center/src/lib/date-utils.ts`):
114	
115	| Days remaining | Color | Label |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| past | Gray | PAST |
118	| 0–7 | Red | URGENT |
119	| 8–13 | Amber | CLOSE |
120	| 14–30 | Yellow | SOON |
121	| 31–60 | Green | IN PROGRESS |
122	| 61+ | Indigo | PLANNING |
123	
124	### Show Archive Logic
125	
126	A show is considered **active** if `dismantleDate ?? moveInDate >= today`; otherwise it is **archived**. There is no explicit archived flag in the DB — the dashboard route computes this dynamically.
127	
128	### DB Schema Key Fields
129	
130	- **shows**: `moveInDate` (required), `dismantleDate`, `advanceWarehouseDate`, `discountDeadline`, `onlineOrderDeadline`, `showStart`, `venue`, `tags` (text array).
131	- **tasks**: completion tracked via `completed` boolean + `completedAt` timestamp; has `category`, `dueDate`, `dueDateRule`, `notes`.
132	- **eblasts**: completion tracked via `sent` boolean + `sentAt` timestamp (not `completed`/`completedAt`); no category field.
133	- **office_tasks**: has `priority` (`low`/`medium`/`high`) and `status` (`todo`/`in-progress`/`done`) fields in addition to `completed`; standalone (no `showId`).
134	- **links**: `title` + `url` only; no completion state.
135	- **venues**: lookup table referenced by `shows.venue` (text, not a foreign key).
136	
137	### Task Categories
138	
139	Tasks belong to one of six hardcoded categories (each has a distinct color and a set of preset templates with calculated due dates):
140	
141	- **Fire Marshal** — deadlines relative to move-in date (calendar and business days)
142	- **ID Sign** — deadlines relative to move-in date
143	- **Warehouse Manifest** — deadlines relative to `advanceWarehouseDate`
144	- **Show Bucket** — deadlines relative to move-in date and `onlineOrderDeadline`
145	- **Vehicle Spotting** — deadlines relative to move-in date
146	- **Electrical** — deadlines relative to `onlineOrderDeadline`
147	
148	The full preset list lives in `artifacts/show-command-center/src/components/task-list.tsx` and `eblast-list.tsx` (same directory). Each preset computes a `dueDate` and stores a human-readable `dueDateRule` string (e.g. `"30 biz days before move-in"`) as display text — it is not re-evaluated after creation.
149	
150	Category badge colors come from `getCategoryColor` in `artifacts/show-command-center/src/lib/date-utils.ts`.
151	
152	### Date Parsing
153	
154	Always use `parseDateStr` from `lib/date-utils.ts` to convert `YYYY-MM-DD` strings to `Date` objects. Using `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` directly parses as UTC midnight and shifts the date backward by one day in US timezones.
155	
156	On the server, `sanitizeDates` in the shows route converts empty-string date fields to `null` before writing to the DB.

## Todoist sync status and guardrails

### Current implementation status

- Phase 1 foundation is in place:
  - `todoist_settings` stores the Task and E-Blast Todoist project IDs server-side.
  - `todoist_sync_events` is the durable outbound outbox schema.
  - `todoist_webhook_events` is the future inbound webhook audit/deduplication schema.
- The application currently still uses the legacy manual one-way Todoist flow:
  - Existing `POST /api/export/todoist/sync` remains active.
  - Existing "Push to Todoist" UI remains active.
  - `tasks.ts` and `eblasts.ts` do not yet enqueue or deliver automatic Todoist events.
  - No Todoist webhook receiver exists yet.
- Do not describe the Phase 1 tables as active automatic synchronization until later phases are implemented.

### Settings

- Todoist project configuration must be read from and written to server-side `todoist_settings`.
- Do not add or restore `localStorage["todoist_prefs"]` as a Todoist sync configuration source.
- This app currently has no user/auth/workspace model, so `todoist_settings` is a singleton keyed by `id = "default"`.

### Outbound sync design

- `todoist_sync_events` is the future durable outbox for task and e-blast changes.
- Use a coalesced current-state model: one active event per item, not a replay of every intermediate edit.
- Delivery shapes are `upsert` and `delete`; `reason` records why the event was created.
- Active means `pending` or `in_progress`. Historical `delivered`, `failed`, and `abandoned` rows must not block future events.
- Never introduce a resident `setInterval` retry loop. This project uses Replit autoscale deployment and can scale to zero between requests.
- Future retries must be triggered by active requests, webhook requests, explicit repair actions, or a deliberately low-frequency scheduled HTTP trigger.

### Deletion and remote identity

- Use `tasks.todoistTaskId` and `eblasts.todoistTaskId` as the only local-to-Todoist identity mappings.
- Never match Todoist tasks by title/content.
- Local deletion will eventually enqueue a retryable remote delete.
- A future Todoist-side deletion must preserve the local task/e-blast record, clear `todoistTaskId`, and log the event as an explicit unlink — never delete the local record and never silently recreate the Todoist task on the next ordinary local edit. Relinking must be an explicit future Sync Health/Repair action, not an implicit side effect of normal outbox delivery.

### Production migration requirement

- Migrations do **not** auto-apply to an already-running deployment: startup only calls the migrator when the `shows` table does not yet exist, so any migration added after initial launch (including `todoist_settings`/`todoist_sync_events`/`todoist_webhook_events`) must be applied manually against the production `DATABASE_URL` via `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run migrate`, then followed by a redeploy/restart to pick up any dependent route changes.

### Key-task name-coupling risk (pre-existing, unrelated to Todoist sync)

- `routes/dashboard.ts`, `routes/shows.ts`, and `task-list.tsx`'s `KEY_TASKS`/`isKeyTask()` identify business-critical tasks (e.g. "Submit To FM/EC", "Submit ID Sign Order", "Bucket Due Date") by exact `{name, category}` string equality, not by a stable id — there is no `presetTaskId` linking a task back to its preset.
- This has already broken production once: `index.ts` contains one-off `UPDATE` statements backfilling renamed task/preset names because key-task detection silently desynced after a label was renamed.
- Any Todoist sync work must resolve local↔remote items only through `todoistTaskId`/local `id`, never through Todoist's `content` string, to avoid reintroducing this same failure mode from the other direction.

 The API server runs DB migrations automatically on startup (via `drizzle-orm/node-postgres/migrator`), but only if the `shows` table does not yet exist — otherwise it skips to avoid re-applying already-applied migrations.
 
+## Todoist sync status and guardrails
+
+### Current implementation status
+
+- Phase 1 foundation is in place:
+  - `todoist_settings` stores the Task and E-Blast Todoist project IDs server-side.
+  - `todoist_sync_events` is the durable outbound outbox schema.
+  - `todoist_webhook_events` is the future inbound webhook audit/deduplication schema.
+- The application currently still uses the legacy manual one-way Todoist flow:
+  - Existing `POST /api/export/todoist/sync` remains active.
+  - Existing "Push to Todoist" UI remains active.
+  - `tasks.ts` and `eblasts.ts` do not yet enqueue or deliver automatic Todoist events.
+  - No Todoist webhook receiver exists yet.
+- Do not describe the Phase 1 tables as active automatic synchronization until later phases are implemented.
+
+### Settings
+
+- Todoist project configuration must be read from and written to server-side `todoist_settings`.
+- Do not add or restore `localStorage["todoist_prefs"]` as a Todoist sync configuration source.
+- This app currently has no user/auth/workspace model, so `todoist_settings` is a singleton keyed by `id = "default"`.
+
+### Outbound sync design
+
+- `todoist_sync_events` is the future durable outbox for task and e-blast changes.
+- Use a coalesced current-state model: one active event per item, not a replay of every intermediate edit.
+- Delivery shapes are `upsert` and `delete`; `reason` records why the event was created.
+- Active means `pending` or `in_progress`. Historical `delivered`, `failed`, and `abandoned` rows must not block future events.
+- Never introduce a resident `setInterval` retry loop. This project uses Replit autoscale deployment and can scale to zero between requests.
+- Future retries must be triggered by active requests, webhook requests, explicit repair actions, or a deliberately low-frequency scheduled HTTP trigger.
+
+### Deletion and remote identity
+
+- Use `tasks.todoistTaskId` and `eblasts.todoistTaskId` as the only local-to-Todoist identity mappings.
+- Never match Todoist tasks by title/content.
+- Local deletion will eventually enqueue a retryable remote delete.
+- A future Todoist-side deletion must preserve the local task/e-blast record, clear `todoistTaskId`, and log the event as an explicit unlink — never delete the local record and never silently recreate the Todoist task on the next ordinary local edit. Relinking must be an explicit future Sync Health/Repair action, not an implicit side effect of normal outbox delivery.
+
+### Production migration requirement
+
+- Migrations do **not** auto-apply to an already-running deployment: startup only calls the migrator when the `shows` table does not yet exist, so any migration added after initial launch (including `todoist_settings`/`todoist_sync_events`/`todoist_webhook_events`) must be applied manually against the production `DATABASE_URL` via `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run migrate`, then followed by a redeploy/restart to pick up any dependent route changes.
+
+### Key-task name-coupling risk (pre-existing, unrelated to Todoist sync)
+
+- `routes/dashboard.ts`, `routes/shows.ts`, and `task-list.tsx`'s `KEY_TASKS`/`isKeyTask()` identify business-critical tasks (e.g. "Submit To FM/EC", "Submit ID Sign Order", "Bucket Due Date") by exact `{name, category}` string equality, not by a stable id — there is no `presetTaskId` linking a task back to its preset.
+- This has already broken production once: `index.ts` contains one-off `UPDATE` statements backfilling renamed task/preset names because key-task detection silently desynced after a label was renamed.
+- Any Todoist sync work must resolve local↔remote items only through `todoistTaskId`/local `id`, never through Todoist's `content` string, to avoid reintroducing this same failure mode from the other direction.
+

message.content:
Implement the narrow Todoist settings update race-condition fix.

Repository:
saygvalentine/GV-Show-Command-Center-TODOIST

Working branch:
expand-completed-tasks-default

Current reviewed commits:
- 761e211a0c2b69114cf1bbeb02e696498542e104
  feat(todoist): add sync outbox foundation and server settings
- b5785f263b09726000469f7b8422cf199178cbc0
  docs: document Todoist sync foundation and guardrails

## Problem to fix

The current `PUT /api/export/todoist/settings` route uses this pattern:

1. Read the current settings row.
2. Merge a partial request body in JavaScript.
3. Upsert the merged object.

That creates a lost-update race when two updates occur close together:

```text
Current:
taskProjectId = A
eblastProjectId = B

Request 1 updates taskProjectId to C.
Request 2 updates eblastProjectId to D.

Both requests read { A, B }.
Request 1 writes { C, B }.
Request 2 writes { A, D }.

Result:
The update to C is lost.
```

## Required design

Replace partial-update semantics with full-document replacement semantics.

### API contract

`PUT /api/export/todoist/settings` must require both properties:

```ts
{
  taskProjectId: string | null;
  eblastProjectId: string | null;
}
```

Rules:

- Both fields are required in the request body.
- Each field may be `null`.
- An empty string from the existing Select UI must still normalize to `null` before validation/upsert.
- The route must not call `readSettings()` before a `PUT`.
- The route must perform one atomic singleton upsert using `id = "default"`.
- `GET` must remain unchanged:
  - Return `{ taskProjectId: null, eblastProjectId: null }` when no row exists.
- The response still returns the full saved settings document.

### Frontend context

Update `TodoistProvider` so each selector update always submits both current values:

- `setTaskProjectId(taskProjectId)` sends:
  ```ts
  {
    taskProjectId,
    eblastProjectId: currentServerOrCachedEblastProjectId
  }
  ```

- `setEblastProjectId(eblastProjectId)` sends:
  ```ts
  {
    taskProjectId: currentServerOrCachedTaskProjectId,
    eblastProjectId
  }
  ```

Requirements:

- Preserve the public context interface:
  - `taskProjectId`
  - `eblastProjectId`
  - `projects`
  - `loadingProjects`
  - `setTaskProjectId`
  - `setEblastProjectId`
- Preserve safe loading behavior: no selector write before server settings have loaded.
- Preserve `"" → null` behavior at the API boundary.
- Do not add optimistic updates unless the existing app pattern clearly requires them.
- After mutation success, keep updating the React Query settings cache with the complete server response.
- Do not retain or restore browser `localStorage["todoist_prefs"]`.

## Files expected to change

Only modify files necessary for this fix. Expected candidates:

- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist-settings.ts`
- `artifacts/show-command-center/src/contexts/todoist-context.tsx`
- `lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml`
- Generated files under:
  - `lib/api-client-react/src/generated/`
  - `lib/api-zod/src/generated/`

If another file is truly required, explain why before modifying it.

## Explicitly out of scope

Do not modify:

- `CLAUDE.md`
- Any database schema or migration.
- `lib/db/migrations/**`
- `lib/db/src/schema/**`
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/tasks.ts`
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/eblasts.ts`
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist.ts`
- Manual sync behavior.
- Existing Push-to-Todoist buttons.
- Outbox processing.
- Webhook routes, webhook verification, raw-body middleware, or Todoist Developer App setup.
- Retry workers, scheduled deployments, cron, polling, or `setInterval`.
- Replit configuration, deployment settings, or secrets.
- Key-task identity cleanup.
- Existing api-zod export-collision/typecheck debt.
- `.claude-user/**`, Playwright output, test artifacts, or unrelated session files.

Do not run a migration.
Do not deploy.
Do not push.
Do not open a pull request.
Do not commit until I explicitly approve.

## Required workflow

### Before editing

1. Show `git status --short`.
2. Show the exact list of files you intend to modify.
3. Explain the old race condition and the new atomic write flow in a short before/after diagram.
4. Confirm no schema or migration change is needed.
5. Confirm that no existing manual Todoist sync behavior will change.

### Implementation requirements

1. Update OpenAPI so the request body requires both nullable project ID fields.
2. Regenerate API client and Zod artifacts using the repository’s normal codegen command.
3. Update the server route:
   - Normalize empty strings to `null`.
   - Validate the complete request body.
   - Make one atomic upsert using `TODOIST_SETTINGS_ID`.
   - Remove application-level `readSettings()` merge logic from `PUT`.
4. Update the context so each setter submits a complete document based on the most recent loaded/cached server settings.
5. Preserve GET defaults and loading protections.

### Verification requirements

After editing:

1. Show `git diff --stat`.
2. Show `git diff --` for every changed non-generated source file.
3. Confirm the request schema rejects:
   - `{}`.
   - `{ taskProjectId: "123" }`.
   - `{ eblastProjectId: "456" }`.
4. Confirm it accepts:
   - `{ taskProjectId: "123", eblastProjectId: "456" }`.
   - `{ taskProjectId: null, eblastProjectId: null }`.
5. Explain why two concurrent full-document writes no longer suffer from the prior **partial-field lost-update** bug.
6. Run the narrowest relevant code generation and type/build checks that are available without touching unrelated known failures.
7. Report any failures and clearly distinguish pre-existing failures from failures caused by this change.
8. Run a targeted secret check on changed files.
9. Show `git status --short`.

Then stop and wait for my review.

Do not stage, commit, push, deploy, run migrations, or begin Phase 2.

## Files I intend to modify

- `lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml` — make both fields required (non-optional, still nullable) on `UpdateTodoistSettingsBody`
- `lib/api-client-react/src/generated/**` — regenerated by codegen
- `lib/api-zod/src/generated/**` — regenerated by codegen
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist-settings.ts` — remove the read-merge-upsert pattern, replace with one atomic full-document upsert
- `artifacts/show-command-center/src/contexts/todoist-context.tsx` — each setter now sends both fields, sourced from the currently loaded/cached settings

No other file is touched.

## Before/after: the race condition

```
BEFORE (read-merge-upsert, partial semantics)
  state: { taskProjectId: A, eblastProjectId: B }

  Req1: setTaskProjectId(C)         Req2: setEblastProjectId(D)
    PUT { taskProjectId: C }          PUT { eblastProjectId: D }
    route reads row → {A, B}          route reads row → {A, B}   ← both read stale state
    merges → {C, B}                   merges → {A, D}
    writes {C, B} ─────────────────────────────┐
                                                  writes {A, D}  ← last write wins, C is lost
  final DB state: { taskProjectId: A, eblastProjectId: D }   ✗ C never persisted

AFTER (full-document replacement, atomic upsert)
  state: { taskProjectId: A, eblastProjectId: B }   (held client-side from the settings query)

  Req1: setTaskProjectId(C)         Req2: setEblastProjectId(D)
    PUT { taskProjectId: C,           PUT { taskProjectId: A,
          eblastProjectId: B }              eblastProjectId: D }
    route: no read — one              route: no read — one
    unconditional upsert               unconditional upsert
    writes {C, B} ──┐            ┌── writes {A, D}
                     └── whichever request's UPDATE commits last in Postgres wins outright ──┘

  final DB state: either { C, B } or { A, D } — never a silently merged/corrupted hybrid,
  and neither field is dropped mid-write by a stale server-side read
```

The fix doesn't make the two concurrent requests resolve to "both edits kept" (that would need optimistic concurrency/versioning, which is out of scope here) — it eliminates the *specific* bug described: the server no longer reads its own stale copy mid-request and merges over it, so the DB can't end up in a state that resulted from combining a stale read with one field from a later write. Whichever request's write lands last simply wins cleanly, with a value the client actually intended to send.

## Confirmations

- **No schema or migration change needed.** `todoist_settings` already has exactly `id`, `task_project_id`, `eblast_project_id`, `updated_at` — full-document replacement is a query-shape change, not a column change.
- **No existing manual Todoist sync behavior changes.** `routes/tasks.ts`, `routes/eblasts.ts`, `routes/todoist.ts`, the "Push to Todoist" buttons, and outbox/webhook code are untouched — this fix is scoped entirely to the settings GET/PUT pair and the context that calls it.

## Why the race is gone

The server no longer performs a read as part of `PUT`. `readSettings()` remains, used only by `GET`. Since the schema now requires both fields, every valid request body is already a complete document — the route does `insert(...).onConflictDoUpdate(...)` directly on `parsed.data`, one atomic statement. Two concurrent requests each carry their own complete, client-assembled snapshot; whichever commits last in Postgres simply becomes the row's value. Nothing in the request path reads a shared prior value and merges over it, so there's no window where a stale read can clobber a field the other request just wrote. On the client, `TodoistProvider` builds that complete snapshot by reading `queryClient.getQueryData` at call time (not a component closure captured at render time), so two changes fired in quick succession each see the other's already-written value rather than a value frozen before either mutation resolved.

The context now reads queryClient.getQueryData() at setter call time, but that cache is only updated in onSuccess. If a user changes the task picker and then immediately changes the e-blast picker before the first PUT returns, the second setter can still read the old cached document and send a full replacement body that restores the old first value.

Required fix:
Add an optimistic React Query cache update and rollback behavior to the Todoist settings mutation flow.

3. On mutation error:

4. Update the setter implementation so every rapid second change reads the optimistically updated current cache and therefore includes the first pending change in its complete replacement request.

```
BEFORE (cache updated only in onSuccess)
  cache: { taskProjectId: A, eblastProjectId: B }

AFTER (onMutate writes the cache immediately, before the network call resolves)
  cache: { taskProjectId: A, eblastProjectId: B }

        cache → { C, B }  immediately, before the PUT even resolves
        PUT { taskProjectId: C, eblastProjectId: B } sent

        saveSettings reads cache → { C, B }   ← sees t0's optimistic value, not stale A
        onMutate fires: snapshots { C, B }, writes cache → { C, D }

  t2  t0's response arrives → onSuccess overwrites cache with server's authoritative { C, B }

  t3  t1's response arrives → onSuccess overwrites cache with server's authoritative { C, D }
        final state: { C, D }   ✓ both edits survive
```

My first pass had a flawed harness (called both setters in the same synchronous tick, no task boundary) — I caught and fixed it, since two real clicks are separate macrotasks and the JS event loop guarantees microtasks (including `onMutate`'s internal `await`) fully drain between them. Corrected result:
```
1. initial cache: { taskProjectId: 'A', eblastProjectId: 'B' }
2. cache immediately after setTaskProjectId(C): { taskProjectId: 'C', eblastProjectId: 'B' }
3. request 2 body actually sent: { taskProjectId: 'C', eblastProjectId: 'D' }
4. ASSERTION request 2 body === { C, D } (not { A, D }): PASS
```

**Rollback demonstration:**
```
cache right after onMutate (optimistic): { taskProjectId: 'C', eblastProjectId: 'B' }
cache after onError rollback: { taskProjectId: 'A', eblastProjectId: 'B' }
ASSERTION rollback restores { A, B }: PASS
```

**Secret scan:** Clean, no matches on the changed file.

**`git status --short`:** Exactly the 6 files from this and the prior approved turn — nothing staged, nothing extra.

## Two judgment calls to flag

1. **No toast added on mutation error.** I checked: no existing toast convention exists for "failed settings writes" specifically (contexts in this app never use `useToast`; the app-wide `toast({..., variant: "destructive"})` pattern lives only in page components for their own mutations). Per your instruction to not add unrelated UI work absent an existing convention, I implemented pure cache rollback with no user-visible error surface. Flagging in case you want one added as a follow-up.

Do not commit yet. The outgoing-request race fix is approved, but the out-of-order response issue you identified must be fixed before this client-side settings change is committed.

Why this is required:

The Todoist context uses the React Query settings cache to construct complete replacement documents. If request 1 is sent first, request 2 is sent second, and request 1’s response arrives last, a blind onSuccess cache replacement from request 1 can overwrite newer optimistic/request-2 state. That can cause a later user interaction to resend stale configuration to the server.

Implement a minimal latest-mutation guard inside TodoistProvider.

## Required behavior

Use a monotonic mutation sequence/version held locally in TodoistProvider, for example with `useRef`.

For every settings mutation:

1. Allocate a sequence number when the mutation begins.
2. In `onMutate`:
   - Record the previous cached settings document.
   - Optimistically write the complete outgoing settings document to the settings query cache.
   - Return mutation context containing:
     - `previous`
     - `sequence`
     - any other minimal data needed.

3. In `onSuccess`:
   - Update the React Query settings cache with the server response only if this mutation’s sequence is still the latest started mutation.
   - If the response belongs to an older mutation, do not let it overwrite newer cached state.

4. In `onError`:
   - Roll back only if this failed mutation is still the latest started mutation.
   - Do not let an older failed mutation roll back a newer optimistic change.
   - If a latest-mutation failure cannot safely restore a known current state, invalidate/refetch the settings query rather than overwriting newer data.

5. Preserve all current requirements:
   - Every request remains a full document with both nullable fields.
   - The context public interface remains unchanged.
   - No localStorage.
   - No schema/migration/API contract/codegen changes.
   - No changes outside the current client-side context file unless TypeScript strictly requires it.
   - No task/eblast/manual sync/outbox/webhook/retry/polling/Phase 2 work.
   - No toast/UI expansion is required.

## Required verification

Provide a focused test or precise executable trace for all three cases:

A. Rapid sequential updates:
- Initial cache { A, B }
- Set task project to C
- Before response, set e-blast project to D
- Assert request 2 body is { C, D }

B. Out-of-order successful responses:
- Request 2 resolves successfully before request 1
- Request 1 then resolves successfully late
- Assert final cache remains { C, D }, not { C, B }

C. Older failure after newer mutation starts:
- Mutation 1 starts and applies optimistic { C, B }
- Mutation 2 starts and applies optimistic { C, D }
- Mutation 1 fails after mutation 2 started
- Assert cache remains { C, D }; it must not roll back to { A, B }

D. Latest mutation failure:
- A single/latest optimistic mutation fails
- Assert cache either restores the correct prior state or safely invalidates/refetches, with the behavior explained.

content.text:
## Migration `0008_public_thanos.sql` — plain-English summary

1. `CREATE TABLE todoist_settings` — a singleton row (`id` text PK, default `'default'`) holding `task_project_id`, `eblast_project_id`, `updated_at`. No data touched.
2. `CREATE TABLE todoist_sync_events` — the outbound outbox: `item_type`, nullable `item_id`, nullable `todoist_task_id`, `operation`, `reason`, `status` (default `'pending'`), `attempt_count` (default `0`), `next_attempt_at` (default `now()`), `claimed_at`, `payload_snapshot` (jsonb), `last_error`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. No data touched.
3. `CREATE TABLE todoist_webhook_events` — inbound audit/dedup log: `provider_event_id`, `fingerprint`, `event_type`, `todoist_task_id`, `payload` (jsonb), `received_at`, `status` (default `'received'`), `processed_at`, `error`. No data touched.
4. Five `CREATE INDEX` statements: a plain `(status, next_attempt_at)` index on the outbox, two **partial unique** indexes on the outbox (`item_active` guarding one active event per live item; `delete_active` guarding one active delete per already-unlinked item), and two indexes on the webhook log (`fingerprint` unique; `provider_event_id` unique where not null).
5. One `INSERT ... SELECT` data migration: copies every row from the pre-existing `todoist_orphans` table into `todoist_sync_events` as a `pending` delete event (`item_id = NULL`, `operation='delete'`, `reason='delete'`), de-duplicated via `DISTINCT` and guarded by `NOT EXISTS` so re-running it is a no-op. **`todoist_orphans` itself is never modified or dropped.**
